d: Four Seasons is powered by our people. We are a collective of individuals who crave to become better, to push ourselves to new heights and to treat each other as we wish to be treated in return. Our team members around the world create amazing experiences for our guests, residents, and partners through a commitment to luxury with genuine heart. We know that the best way to enable our people to deliver these exceptional guest experiences is through a world-class employee experience and company culture.

The Pool & Beach Assistant Server supports the service team by ensuring guests receive exceptional, attentive, and personalized service throughout their poolside and beach experience. The role involves assisting with food and beverage delivery, maintaining cleanliness and organization of service areas, and anticipating guest needs with professionalism and enthusiasm.
q: Previous experience in Food & Beverage service, hospitality, or customer service is preferred.
Positive attitude with a genuine passion for guest service.
Ability to work efficiently in a fast-paced outdoor environment.
Team-oriented mindset with a willingness to learn.
Ability to stand, walk, and carry trays or service items for extended periods.
Flexibility to work weekends, holidays, and varying shifts.
Good command of spoken English; additional languages are an advantage.
Ability to anticipate guest needs and exceed expectations.
Professional, reliable, and adaptable approach to work.
If you are passionate about hospitality and enjoy working in a dynamic beachfront environment, we would love to hear from you.🌊☀️🏖️
r: li
Assist servers in delivering food, beverages, and amenities to guests at the pool and beach.
li
Set up, maintain, and clean service stations throughout the shift.
li
Ensure all pool and beach areas are clean, organized, and guest-ready at all times.
li
Replenish supplies, linens, menus, condiments, and service equipment as needed.
li
Clear tables, remove used items promptly, and reset seating areas efficiently.
li
Respond to guest requests in a timely and courteous manner.
li
Communicate effectively with servers, bartenders, kitchen staff, and supervisors to ensure smooth operations.
li
Demonstrate thorough knowledge of menu offerings and resort facilities.
li
Follow all food safety, hygiene, and health and safety standards.
li
Assist with opening and closing duties as assigned.
li
Maintain a professional appearance and demeanor at all times.

The Speech and Language Pathologist is responsible for assessing, diagnosing, and treating patients with speech, language, voice, communication, and swallowing disorders. The role plays a vital part in supporting long-term care patients, including those with neurological, developmental, and acquired conditions, to maximize their functional communication and swallowing abilities, thereby enhancing their quality of life.
q: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Speech and Language Pathology / Speech Therapy from a recognized university.
Valid professional license/registration to practice in Bahrain (NHRA license) or eligibility to obtain one.
Minimum 6 years’ experience as a Speech and Language Pathologist, preferably in a hospital or long-term care setting.
Experience in managing adult neurological conditions (e.g., stroke, traumatic brain injury, Parkinson’s, dementia) is highly desirable.
Strong diagnostic and clinical reasoning skills.
Empathy, patience, and excellent communication skills.
Ability to educate and support patients, caregivers, and staff effectively.
Team player with collaborative approach in a multidisciplinary care environment.
Commitment to evidence-based practice and continuous learning.
r: li
Assess and diagnose communication, speech, language, and swallowing disorders in patients across all age groups.
li
Develop individualized treatment plans tailored to each patient’s needs, goals, and medical condition.
li
Deliver evidence-based therapy for patients with communication difficulties (e.g., aphasia, dysarthria, apraxia, stuttering, voice disorders).
li
Manage and treat swallowing disorders (dysphagia), including conducting bedside and instrumental swallowing assessments.
li
Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams (physicians, nurses, physiotherapists, occupational therapists, dietitians, and psychologists) to ensure comprehensive patient care.
li
Educate and counsel patients, families, and caregivers on therapy goals, home programs, and communication strategies.
li
Document assessments, treatment plans, progress notes, and outcome measures accurately in the hospital’s medical record system.
li
Participate in case conferences, family meetings, and care planning discussions.
li
Support training and development of nursing staff and caregivers in managing communication and swallowing issues.
li
Stay up to date with advances in speech-language pathology practices and participate in continuous professional development.
li
Ensure compliance with Bahrain health regulations, ethical standards, and hospital policies.
